section_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. (Corresponds to Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860). Classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by Magistrate of the First Class.

section_title: Definition of Cheating and General Punishment
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to cheat. Whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. (Corresponds to Section 415 & 417 of the Indian Penal Code). Classification: Non-Cognizable, Bailable.

section_title: Criminal Breach of Trust
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, commits criminal breach of trust. Punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both. (Corresponds to Section 405 & 406 of the Indian Penal Code). Classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable.

section_title: Theft and Community Service for Petty Theft
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both: Provided that in cases of theft where the value of stolen property is less than five thousand rupees, and a person is convicted for the first time, upon return of the value of property or restoration of the stolen property, shall be punished with community service. (Corresponds to Section 378 & 379 IPC). Classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable.

section_title: Extortion and Blackmail
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person, or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property or valuable security, commits extortion. Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. (Corresponds to Section 383 & 384 IPC). Classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by Magistrate of the First Class.

section_title: Criminal Intimidation and Death Threats
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, commits criminal intimidation. Simple intimidation: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both. Threat to cause death or grievous hurt or destruction of property by fire: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. (Corresponds to Section 503 & 506 IPC).

section_title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt and Grievous Hurt
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Section 115(2): Whoever voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both. (Corresponds to Section 323 IPC; Bailable, Non-Cognizable). Section 117(2): Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt (fracture, dislocation of bone, permanent damage to eye/ear/face, bodily pain for twenty days) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. (Corresponds to Section 325 IPC; Cognizable, Bailable).

section_title: Rash Driving on a Public Way
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. (Corresponds to Section 279 of the Indian Penal Code). Classification: Cognizable, Bailable, Triable by Any Magistrate.

section_title: Causing Death by Negligence and Hit-and-Run
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Section 106(1): Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. Section 106(2): Whoever causes the death of any person by rash and negligent driving of vehicle not amounting to culpable homicide, and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description of a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. (Corresponds to Section 304A IPC). Classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable under 106(2).

section_title: Husband or Relative of Husband Subjecting Woman to Cruelty
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Cruelty means: (a) Any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical); or (b) Harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security. (Corresponds to Section 498A IPC). Classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable. Note: Under BNSS Section 35(3) and Supreme Court ruling in Arnesh Kumar, notice to appear must precede any arrest.

section_title: Defamation and Community Service Option
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service. Defamation consists of making or publishing any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person. (Corresponds to Section 499 & 500 IPC). Classification: Non-Cognizable, Bailable.

section_title: Forgery and Forgery for Purpose of Cheating
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)
text: Section 336: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Section 338: Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. (Corresponds to Section 465 & 468 IPC). Classification: 338 is Cognizable and Non-Bailable.

section_title: Notice of Appearance before Police Officer (Formerly Section 41A CrPC)
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023)
text: Section 35(3): The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under sub-section (1) (offences punishable with imprisonment up to seven years), issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, to appear before him or at such other place as may be specified in the notice. Where such a notice is issued, it shall be the duty of that person to comply with the terms of the notice. Where such person complies and continues to comply with the notice, he shall not be arrested in respect of the offence referred to in the notice unless, for reasons to be recorded in writing, the police officer is of the opinion that he ought to be arrested.

section_title: Information in Cognizable Cases and Zero FIR
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023)
text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge of a police station (Zero FIR). If given electronically, it shall be taken on record and signed within three days by the informant. If the officer in charge of a police station refuses to record the information, the person aggrieved may send the substance of such information, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police concerned. (Corresponds to Section 154 CrPC).

section_title: Application to Magistrate upon Police Refusal to Lodge FIR
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023)
text: Any person aggrieved by a refusal by police officer to investigate or register FIR under Section 173, may make an application to the Magistrate having jurisdiction, accompanied by an affidavit stating that application was earlier made to the Superintendent of Police under Section 173(4). The Magistrate, after considering the application and affidavit, may order the police to investigate. (Corresponds to Section 156(3) CrPC).

section_title: Direction for Grant of Bail to Person Apprehending Arrest (Anticipatory Bail)
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023)
text: Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction under this section that in the event of such arrest, he shall be released on bail. The Court considers nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent criminal record, possibility of applicant fleeing from justice, and whether accusation has been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant. (Corresponds to Section 438 CrPC).

section_title: Mandatory Rights of Arrested Persons
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023)
text: Section 47: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout interrogation. Section 48: Right of arrested person to have one relative or friend informed of his arrest and location where he is detained. Section 53: Examination of arrested person by medical officer immediately after arrest. The police officer making the arrest shall prepare a memorandum of arrest attested by at least one witness and countersigned by the arrested person.

section_title: Admissibility of Electronic Records and Certificate
source: IndiaCode: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Act No. 47 of 2023)
text: Section 61: Nothing in this Adhiniyam shall apply to deny the admissibility of an electronic record in evidence on the ground that it is an electronic record. Section 63: Any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media shall be deemed to be also a document. A certificate identifying the electronic record, describing the manner in which it was produced, and signed by a person in official charge or management of relevant device, shall be evidence of any matter stated in the certificate. (Corresponds to Section 65B of Indian Evidence Act).

section_title: Dishonour of Cheque for Insufficiency of Funds in the Account
source: IndiaCode: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (Act No. 26 of 1881)
text: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person for the discharge of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of insufficiency of funds or exceeding agreement amount, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both. Mandatory conditions: (a) Cheque presented within three months; (b) Demand for payment made by giving notice in writing within thirty days of the receipt of information from the bank; (c) Drawer fails to make payment within fifteen days of receipt of said notice.

section_title: Identity Theft and Cheating by Personation Using Computer Resource
source: IndiaCode: Information Technology Act, 2000 (Act No. 21 of 2000)
text: Section 66C: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh. Section 66D: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource, cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees. Frequently charged alongside Section 318(4) BNS for cyber financial scams.

section: Section 12 Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
section_title: Application to Magistrate for Protection, Residence, and Monetary Relief
source: IndiaCode: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (Act No. 43 of 2005)
text: An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act. Reliefs include Protection Orders against acts of violence (Section 18), Residence Orders prohibiting dispossession from shared household (Section 19), Monetary Relief for medical expenses and maintenance (Section 20), Custody Orders for children (Section 21), and Compensation Orders (Section 22). The Magistrate shall fix the first date of hearing within three days and endeavour to dispose of the application within sixty days.
